cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: the 1st percentile of the F distribution with 6 and 4 degrees of freedom
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes '=F.INV(A2,A3,A4)' over the data 0.01 / 6 / 4 with the result 0.10930991. Re-derived independently by solving P(F <= x) = 0.01 with mpmath's root finder over the regularized incomplete beta function at 50 digits: x = 0.10930991412457853874, i.e. exactly the published 0.10930991 at 8 dp. Note this is the LEFT-tailed inverse -- the page's own identity is "If p = F.DIST(x,...), then F.INV(p,...) = x" -- which is what separates it from F.INV.RT, whose page publishes 15.20686 for the identical arguments.

Excel documents: "If probability < 0 or probability > 1, F.INV returns the #NUM! error value." EXECUTED RESULT: all four LibreOffice builds (24.2.0.3, 24.8.7.2, 25.2.0.3, 25.8.7.3) return #VALUE! here instead of the documented #NUM! -- the same systemic #VALUE!-substitution pattern already recorded across this corpus, an error-code difference rather than a computation one.
